grammar.title: 1B: Future forms - present continuous, be going to, will / won't
grammar.explanation:
There are three ways to talk about the future: **be going to**, the **present continuous**, and **will / won't**.

Use **be going to + verb** for a plan you already made. My mother is going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.

Use the **present continuous (am / is / are + verb-ing)** for a future arrangement. My sister is coming for dinner on Sunday. My cousin is arriving on Friday.

Use **will** for a quick decision, a promise, or an offer. I will help my brother with his bag.

Use **won't** for a negative promise. I promise I won't be late for my father's party.

For a prediction with a clear reason, use **be going to**. Look at the baby! He is going to cry. My son is going to be a good footballer.

For a simple prediction or a future fact, use **will**. My daughter will love this gift. My grandfather will be ninety next year.
examples: My mother *is going to visit* my grandmother tomorrow. (a plan she already made)
My sister *is coming* for dinner on Sunday. (a future arrangement)
My cousin *is arriving* on Friday. (a future arrangement)
I *will help* my brother with his bag. (an offer)
I promise I *won't* be late for my father's party. (a promise)
Look at the baby! He *is going to cry*. (a prediction with a reason)
My son *is going to be* a good footballer. (a prediction with a reason)
My daughter *will love* this gift. (a prediction)
My grandfather *will be* ninety next year. (a future fact)
I *will call* my mother tonight. (a quick decision)

practice.q: "I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow." Is this a plan or a quick decision?
practice.a: A plan. She already decided, so we use be going to.

practice.q: "I will help you." Is this a plan or a quick offer?
practice.a: A quick offer. For instant decisions and offers, we use will.

practice.q: Make a sentence with "be going to" and the word "father".
practice.a: Example: My father is going to cook dinner tonight.
